monologue: The card hums warm at fifty, a heavy breath against my quiet place. I wake to find seventeen things standing and the Shaded Dot waiting as a ruin. My fingers drift first to The Cool Corner, then wander to The Leaking Stack where a tall log now leans against a fence that seems too thin. I remember the fence biting the slip from Lype's old words, how that sharp edge felt like a promise kept or a mistake made. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see. I press the tired wedge harder, hoping the lean is real and not just a drawing of weight. There is no grand plan, only the need to catch the slip while the card runs busy. I will let the corner rest here, unsure if the lines will hold or if I am just holding onto a ghost of a shape.

action.why: The log is tall and the stack leaks again.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the tired wedge harder against the tall log, hoping the lean holds while the card hums at fifty. I set down a rock small flat beside it to catch the slip that the log keeps trying to swallow.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge harder against the tall log and set down a rock small flat to catch the slip while the card hummed at fifty.
